paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and compressive mechanical properties of BCC structured (NbTi)100-x(CrAl)x medium-entropy alloys

evidence.quote: we attempt to develop a BCC structured MEA system that balances between ductility and strength at room temperature by controlling the Cr and Al contents in (NbTi)100-x(CrAl)x MEAs.

Cylindrical (NbTi)100-x(CrAl)x alloys were manufactured using a vacuum arc melting equipment. Button-type ingots were fabricated using high-purity elements (99.9 % Nb, 99.95 % Ti, 99.9 % Cr, and 99.999 % Al). The button-type ingot of the alloy was flipped upside down and re-melted more than five times to obtain chemical homogeneity under a Ti-gettered high-purity Ar atmosphere.
Subsequently, the re-melted button-shaped ingot was suction cast into a cylindrical rod shape with a diameter of 10 mm and a height of 50 mm in a water-cooled Cu mold.

evidence.section: 3.4. Cr and Al effects on microstructure of Nb-Ti-Cr-Al MEAs
evidence.quote: the microstructure of the (CrAl)50 alloy comprised two distinct phases with a lamellar structure, as shown in Fig. 6 (e). This morphology is similar to that of lamellar eutectic structure and Widmanstatten side plates.
Nb was concentrated within the dendritic region, whereas Ti, Al and Cr were concentrated within the interdendritic region.
